verdict.rationale: Sumsub documents configurable verification levels as sequences of steps, an AI level builder that creates levels from plain-language descriptions, client lists for building verification flows, and SDK text and branding changes you can preview before going live. Together these point to no-code template and flow configuration. However, the evidence never documents conditional step logic, risk-based routing, or country-specific requirement rules. missing for 10: documented conditional/branching steps, risk-based routing rules, country-specific requirement configuration, explicit confirmation that changes deploy without engineering, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops lead, I can configure verification logic without code — conditional steps, risk-based routing, country-specific requirements, and template changes that don't need an engineering deploy

citations.quote: A level is a sequence of steps that your applicants have to take to verify their identity.
It helps you create and configure verification levels quickly and effortlessly by just describing your requirements in plain language.
With client lists, you can manage flexible sets of keys to create verification flows and transaction monitoring rules
With SDK text, you can change the default wording your applicants see during verification — instructions, button labels, error messages, email templates, and more.
add step-level instructions and tips, and preview the result before going live.
